clue.text: Report of people in A&E? What they'll need, waiting!

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for the people is said out loud to give a different spelling

parts.note: those being treated in a hospital's Accident and Emergency department are patients

explanation.surface: A comment on the long waits endured by people sitting in a hospital casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm tolerance of delay is exactly the virtue anyone stuck in a waiting room requires.

clue.text: Agent set up to probe mean tricks moves quickly

indicators.note: to probe is to go into something, so the agent's letters go inside the tricks

parts.note: mean tricks are scams, swindles

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: a sales agent is a rep

explanation.surface: An undercover agent is planted to investigate shabby frauds and then makes a quick getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry or dash about briskly, like a small animal, is a synonym of moving fast.

clue.text: Why rats could be dark-looking

indicators.note: could be says these letters might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: An explanation of why rodents might appear dark in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarthy complexion is a dark one, so the adjective is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lecturer maybe in laboratory

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A lecturer might well be found in a science laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer is one example of a public speaker, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Ministers soon restricted by Civil Service

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: anon is an old word meaning soon

explanation.surface: Government ministers will shortly find their freedom curbed by the civil service bureaucracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are ministers of religion, and canons are clergy attached to a cathedral.

clue.text: Authorisation for investigation coming from chaser around with battle cry?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: a battle is fighting, war
to rant is to cry out loudly and angrily

explanation.surface: A pursuer with a war cry seems to be getting official permission to investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a position word but is the anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Police need a court document granting authority before they may examine private premises.

clue.text: Railway official resorting to steam trains

indicators.note: re-sorting means sorting again, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A railway official turns back to old steam engines.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a railway station is a classic railway official.

clue.text: I ate hot old hen, nasty dish

indicators.note: nasty suggests these letters have been treated badly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalls eating an unpleasant meal of hot elderly chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a British dish of sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional British meal, so it is an example of a dish.

clue.text: Form of cruelty — unhappy maiden is being imprisoned

indicators.note: something imprisoned is shut inside, so the word is goes within the other letters

parts.note: unhappy means sad
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A sad young woman is locked up, a cruel situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking pleasure in inflicting pain on others is a particular kind of cruelty.

clue.text: Reasonable declaration looks phony with December passing

indicators.note: something that looks phony is not what it seems, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A statement seems false once a December date is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with December passing' takes DEC out of DECLARATION, and 'looks phony' rearranges the remaining LARATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensible, logical thinking is reasonable, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Male or female head, not English

indicators.note: not English means the abbreviation for English is removed

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head

explanation.surface: A head of either sex, specifically not an English one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat is a name used both for men (Patrick) and women (Patricia).

clue.text: Fellow looking forward to the match

definitions.text: Fellow looking forward to the match

parts.words: Fellow looking forward to the match
parts.note: seems a sports fan eager for a game, but the match is a wedding and the fellow is the man engaged

explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests football, but here it means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A man engaged to be married eagerly awaits his wedding, the match.

clue.text: Severity of mess around road — I start to protest

indicators.note: the mess goes around the road, so its letters enclose the abbreviation

parts.note: to make a hash of something is to make a mess

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A protester complains about how badly a road has been botched.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity of conditions means suffering or privation, a fair synonym.

clue.text: Party in which to see upper-class couple

indicators.note: the party is where the upper-class letter is seen, so it goes inside

parts.note: a do is a party
U stands for upper-class in British usage

explanation.surface: A party where you can spot a posh pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of performers or partners is a two-person group.

clue.text: Like something a poet's written or the opposite

definitions.meaning: a poem is written in lines with metre, not prose
an opposite or reverse of something

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer describes poetry; as one word it means reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it means contrary; split in two it describes poetic form.

clue.text: Regret Aussie beast being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the word is spoken, giving a different spelling with the same sound

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, an Australian animal

explanation.surface: Someone regrets an Australian animal being listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to wish it undone, a direct synonym of regretting.

clue.text: Advertise concert with note that has name missing

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

indicators.note: missing says the letter for name is taken away from the note

explanation.surface: Publicising a concert with a written note that omits a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To publicise or push a product is to advertise it.

clue.text: A moving sort of entertainment?

parts.note: moving suggests touching emotionally, but it means travelling from place to place

explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' seems to mean emotionally stirring; really it means a touring show.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring broadcast or show that travels between venues is literally a moving entertainment.

clue.text: Horse at home eating a huge quantity

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the letter a goes within

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A horse in its stable munching through an enormous amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge heap of anything, such as a pile of paperwork, is figuratively a large mass.

clue.text: Slow up, being restricted by explosive chemical

indicators.note: being restricted means being confined within the other piece

parts.note: HE is high explosive

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: slow means tardy

explanation.surface: Something slow is held up by an explosive chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, high explosive, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound containing water molecules is a kind of chemical.

clue.text: Provincial giant has one belief to fight for — against wife always!

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a cause is a principle worth fighting for
ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A countryside giant fights for a cause, always opposed to his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The Giant's Causeway is a famous rock formation in Northern Ireland, often called the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant of legend is Finn McCool, whose basalt road on the Antrim coast bears his name.

clue.text: The female wanting love but denied love is put off

parts.note: she means the female

indicators.note: denied means the second love is refused, so its letter is removed

parts.note: O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A woman who wants romance but is refused it gets brushed off.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone or set aside a plan is to put it off.

clue.text: Tennis tournament Don avoids — it can be boring

indicators.note: avoids says the name Don is kept out of the tournament's name

parts.note: the grass-court championship held each summer in south-west London

explanation.surface: A man named Don stays away from a dull tennis event.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimlet is a hand tool for drilling, so it is literally boring holes.

clue.text: A source of inspiration, daughter venturing a smile?

parts.note: a muse inspires artists

explanation.surface: A daughter's muse inspires her to try a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tickled enough to try a grin is entertained.

clue.text: Theologian embracing a member of the family

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside, so the letter a goes within

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A theologian hugs one of their relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is a relative within the family.

clue.text: Flag of monarch placed by watercourse

indicators.note: placed by means set next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a stream is a small watercourse
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal flag is planted beside a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pennant is a kind of flag.

clue.text: It includes humour? Some miss it completely

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grumble that some people completely fail to see the joke in a comedy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a television series built around humour.

clue.text: I love routines, indisposed to change completely

indicators.note: indisposed means out of sorts, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone who loves their routines is reluctant to transform everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform something radically is to overhaul it entirely.
